issue.title: test_capacity_gate_to_admission: land segment has queue_weight None where tests expect 2.0 (2 nodes fail at master 244442ee8)
issue.description:
Two tests in tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py fail deterministically at master
244442ee8: test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission (assert land.queue_weight
== 2.0, got None, line 152) and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget
(same None-vs-2.0 assertion shape). The rendered `bd/land_epic` segment expands to
PromptDirectives with queue_weight=None and queue_weight_explicit unset, i.e. the land
segment carries no explicit queue weight when the test expects one.

Found 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_31 while verifying an unrelated change; the
test-scoped lane failed on these two nodes and they fail with the node run alone (~3s).

Attribution attempted, not resolved: run per commit in a detached worktree with
PYTHONPATH pointing at it, the failure is present at 244442ee8, 9cfb06a54, 9231c9352,
65c8169f9 and e65cc22ee, so it predates the five most recent commits; the test file was
last touched by 89d51301f ("feat: adopt queue capacity budget adapters"). The six
sase-core commits between the pinned sase-core-revision.txt and the linked checkout used
by this workspace's build (tool-run fingerprints, fleet catalog, gateway capability) do
not touch queue weights, so core skew is unlikely but not excluded. It is also not ruled
out that the workspace's installed plugins or user xprompt config change how
bd/land_epic expands; whoever picks this up should first confirm it reproduces on a
clean CI checkout, then find where the land directive's queue weight is supposed to be
applied (%queue directive wiring landed in 0770357cd).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails on every run and alone (~3s), and at all five most recent commits checked in detached worktrees; the assertion is a fixed None-vs-2.0 comparison with no timing or ordering dependence. A rerun on the same tree never passed.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_33 at clean master 86ff62c08 (also with my 2-file diff stashed): tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and ::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget both fail deterministically in isolation with 'assert None == 2.0' on land.queue_weight. Surfaced when the diff-scoped lane escalated to the full suite during sase-iu.

Independently reproduced on a stashed-clean tree at master 86ff62c08: both tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and ::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget fail with `assert None == 2.0` (PromptDirectives.queue_weight is None). Deterministic, also reproduces in isolation with xdist disabled.

Independent reproduction (2026-09-20, service_git_credentials plan work): both test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget fail with `assert None == 2.0` on land.queue_weight, identically with my change applied and with it stashed on clean master 52b028394, each also failing when run alone. Impact: forces the full scoped lane red for any change that escalates it.

Independent reproduction as sase-135 land agent on clean master 9a56fc1294 (workspace sase_10): tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and ::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget both fail with 'assert None == 2.0' at land.queue_weight. Reproduced twice — once in a full 'just test' (43708 passed, 5 failed, 17m38s) and again in the full-escalated 'just test-scoped' lane (43710 passed, 3 failed, 13m19s) — and once in isolation, so it is deterministic, not a flake. Root cause is 28d1e87083 ('feat: make just check-full explicit-only for agents'), whose commit message states 'Epic landers drop %q(w=2.0) and claim the default capacity unit'; that commit updated tests/test_bead_xprompt_tags.py and tests/test_work_queue_capacity.py but left tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py asserting the old 2.0 land weight. Unrelated to epic sase-135. Note sase-13o appears to be the same defect filed separately.

Independently reproduced 2026-09-20 on host apollo, workspace sase_17, master 624a29ea72: both test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget fail identically with an unrelated working-tree change stashed and applied, so this is not a workspace-specific artefact of one agent.

Independently reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_19 at master e99bd48ac4: test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget both fail with 'assert land.queue_weight == 2.0' (got None), in the scoped lane and again in a targeted run on a clean tree (my diff stashed). The sase-core-rs extension in this workspace was rebuilt from the linked sase-core checkout (0.34.68) by just check just before the run, so a stale extension does not explain it.

Independently reproduced during a sase-11y.8 rebase-conflict repair: both test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget fail with 'assert None == 2.0' (land queue_weight) in isolation and in the diff-scoped lane, and identically on a detached checkout of pristine origin/master 68d9e0f65 (PYTHONPATH pointed at that tree's src), so unrelated to the sase-11y.8 oneshot-proc changes.

Independently reproduced 2026-09-20 at master HEAD 15763853b (workspace sase_10): tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission fails 'assert land.queue_weight == 2.0' with None, and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget also fails. Deterministic, not a flake: failed in the full 'just test-scoped' run, again in a targeted rerun, and again with my working-tree changes stashed (pristine HEAD), so my docs/YAML diff is not the cause. Sibling bead sase-13o reports the same defect.

payload.entry:
CLOSED AS DUPLICATE (2026-09-20 triage). Same defect, same two nodes, same assertion as sase-13o: tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and ::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget both failing 'assert None == 2.0' on land.queue_weight. sase-13o was filed at 12:03:07Z and this bead at 12:07:58Z, so sase-13o is the canonical report; its own +1 from sase-zr.7.land had already identified this bead as a same-day duplicate.

No evidence is lost: this bead's unique content -- the detached-worktree replay showing the failure at all five of 244442ee8, 9cfb06a54, 9231c9352, 65c8169f9 and e65cc22ee, the 8 independent corroborations, and the pointer that %queue wiring landed in 0770357cd -- is carried forward as a note on sase-13o, together with the root cause found during this triage (src/sase/bead/work.py's _queue_capacity_lines never passes a weight to format_queue_directive). The defect is still live at master ec7dbbfdf and the fix is tracked on sase-13o. Do not corroborate this bead; put further evidence on sase-13o.

payload.close_reason: Duplicate of sase-13o, which reported the same two nodes and the same assertion 4m51s earlier

evidence.note: Independent reproduction 2026-09-20 on origin/master ec7dbbfdf (workspace sase_32): both tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission and ::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget fail with `assert None == 2.0`, where None is the queue_weight of PromptDirectives(auto_mode='plan', model='large', ...). They fail in the escalated full lane (rule core-identity-changed), fail again in isolation, and fail identically with all local changes stashed, so not a flake and not caused by my diff. Sibling task sase-13o reports the same two nodes.
